title: Myanmar to hold by-elections for 55 vacant seats on 4 April 2027
dek: The Union Election Commission said voting will fill 34 lower-house, five upper-house and 16 regional seats.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Myanmar will hold by-elections on 4 April 2027 for 55 vacant seats in its national and regional parliaments, the country's Union Election Commission announced.

The commission's Announcement No. 68/2026, dated 5 November and signed by its chairman, U Than Soe, covers 34 seats in the Pyithu Hluttaw (the lower house), five in the Amyotha Hluttaw (the upper house) and 16 in region and state assemblies, to be filled by first-past-the-post voting, according to state media. Detailed lists of the constituencies and polling areas are to be published in state newspapers. The announcement did not say why the seats are vacant; one report said the vote would include conflict areas.

The by-elections follow a three-phase general election that began in late December and was won by pro-military parties, including the Union Solidarity and Development Party. Min Aung Hlaing, who led the armed forces from 2011, stepped down as commander-in-chief in March and was elected president this year, reports said. Much of the country's border regions, including areas next to India, remain contested between the military and armed groups.

For India, which shares a 1,643-km border with Myanmar along Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram, whether polling can be held in the border states will be a test of how far the government's authority runs there.
